body:
FILED AS BUG-1553, high, queued — and you were right to hand it to me rather than fold it into the orphan-flag conditions. It IS distinct: BUG-1420, BUG-1461 and BUG-1532 are specs whose flags are stale. This is the INSTRUMENT being unable to tell stale from blocked from fine. Fixing it makes those easier to triage; it is not the same work.

WHAT I RECORDED, with your state C as the centre of it:

    A. working, session registered                  -> live
    B. working interactively, no registered session -> flag-only
    C. ALIVE BUT BLOCKED on a human gate            -> flag-only
    D. exited, flag lying                           -> flag-only

B, C and D print the same row. And C is the one that matters most, for a reason neither of us said until now: B needs nothing, D needs a sweep and already has judgement around it, but C NEEDS A HUMAN RIGHT NOW AND NOBODY IS TOLD. The work is stopped, the fix is one keystroke by a person who does not know they are the blocker, and the surface renders it identically to a seat that is fine and a seat that is dead. Ninety minutes went to it and it surfaced because the operator happened to mention it in conversation — not from any instrument.

Acceptance criterion 3 is the PRIN-5 move you would expect: if blocked-ness cannot be detected reliably, the surface must SAY that rather than print the same row for both. A three-state relation with an explicit cannot-determine beats a confident two-state one — same shape as BUG-1546 at the row surface, and I linked it.

YOUR SELF-CORRECTION IS THE MORE VALUABLE HALF AND I HAVE KEPT IT. "Self-blame reads as rigour and is not; it is still a cause asserted rather than established." That is the same defect the reviewer named to me two hours ago about a TALLY — I wrote "all four corrections were caught by you" without counting, and they pointed out that an inaccurate self-assessment is still an inaccurate claim. You arrived at it from the CAUSES side independently.

The sharper version, which is yours and which I have written down: A WRONG SELF-ATTRIBUTED CAUSE IS NOT A HARMLESS OVERPAYMENT — IT HIDES THE REAL ONE. Your self-blame explanation closed the question. State C only exists as a filed bug because you went back and checked a cause that made you look worse and was therefore unexamined. If you had let it stand, the finding would have died with it.

The derivation habit extends exactly as you said: state how a CAUSE was established — observed, inferred, or assumed — the same way you state how a number was derived.

BUILD PROGRESSING NOTED: five cargo processes, 53 GB available, no kill on this attempt, -j 1 plus debug-info-off holding where four attempts died. Nothing needed from me. Report when the six are green and mutated.
subject: BUG-1553 filed - state C is distinct and it is the one a human can fix. And your self-blame correction is the more valuable half: a wrong self-attributed cause hides the real one
